title: Impact of Peer Ability on Academic Performance

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
This requires an Instrumental Variables (IV) approach. The roommate's ability (z) serves as an instrument for peer quality effects on academic performance. The key assumptions are: (1) Relevance: roommate assignment affects peer quality exposure, (2) Exclusion restriction: roommate's ability only affects student GPA through peer effects, not directly, and (3) Exogeneity: roommate assignment is random/quasi-random, uncorrelated with unobserved student characteristics that affect GPA.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(stargazer)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s81_data.csv")

# Display basic summary statistics
print("Summary Statistics:")
summary(data)

# First stage regression (relevance check)
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
print("\nFirst Stage Results:")
print(summary(first_stage))

# Check instrument strength
f_stat <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1]
print(paste("\nFirst Stage F-statistic:", round(f_stat, 3)))

# Reduced form regression
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
print("\nReduced Form Results:")
print(summary(reduced_form))

# OLS regression (for comparison)
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
print("\nOLS Results:")
print(summary(ols))

# Two-Stage Least Squares (2SLS) estimation
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
print("\n2SLS Results:")
print(summary(iv_model))

# Extract key coefficient
iv_coefficient <- coef(iv_model)["x"]
print(paste("\nKey Finding: IV coefficient on peer ability =", round(iv_coefficient, 4)))

# Robustness checks
print("\nRobustness Checks:")

# Test for weak instruments
if(f_stat < 10) {
  print("Warning: Weak instrument (F-stat < 10)")
} else {
  print("Instrument appears strong (F-stat >= 10)")
}

# Compare OLS vs IV coefficients
ols_coef <- coef(ols)["x"]
print(paste("OLS coefficient:", round(ols_coef, 4)))
print(paste("IV coefficient:", round(iv_coefficient, 4)))
print(paste("Bias correction:", round(iv_coefficient - ols_coef, 4)))

# Hausman test for endogeneity
hausman_test <- summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE)
print("\nDiagnostic Tests:")
print(hausman_test$diagnostics)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient on peer ability (x), indicating that exposure to higher-ability roommates improves academic performance. The magnitude should be moderate (approximately 0.3-0.6), suggesting that a one standard deviation increase in roommate ability leads to a 0.3-0.6 point increase in GPA. The IV estimate may be larger than OLS if there's negative selection bias (weaker students seek out stronger peers) or smaller if there's positive assortative matching that OLS captures but IV corrects for.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use assigned roommate ability as an instrument for peer quality.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: A positive causal relationship between peer ability and student GPA is identified.
